tieu_de: Venus retrograde and Mars retrograde: what they are and how to read them
mo: How to read a retrograde transit
Born with Venus or Mars retrograde
Check the transits against your chart

Mercury retrograde gets the headlines three or four times a year. Venus and Mars go retrograde far less often, and that rarity is exactly why they matter more when they do. A Venus or Mars retrograde parks a personal planet in one stretch of the zodiac for months, and whatever it touches in your chart gets worked over slowly and repeatedly.

This guide explains what's actually happening in the sky, how the two cycles differ, how to read them as transits against your own chart, and what it means if you were born with one of them retrograde.

doan: No planet ever reverses in its orbit. Retrograde motion is a line-of-sight effect: from Earth, a planet appears to slow down, stop, drift backward against the zodiac for a while, stop again, and then resume forward motion.
The cause differs for the two planets.

Mars is outside Earth's orbit. Earth moves faster, so roughly every two years we catch up with Mars and overtake it on the inside track. While we pass, Mars appears to slide backward, the way a slower car on the highway seems to drift back as you overtake it. Mid-retrograde, Earth sits between the Sun and Mars: Mars is opposite the Sun, closest to us, and at its brightest.

Venus is inside Earth's orbit and moves faster than we do. Its retrograde happens when Venus swings around its orbit and passes between Earth and the Sun. Mid-retrograde, Venus is conjunct the Sun (the inferior conjunction), and it switches from being an evening star, visible after sunset, to a morning star, visible before dawn.

The points where the motion appears to stop are called stations: the station retrograde and the station direct. A planet at a station is moving so slowly that it sits on nearly the same degree for days, which is why stations are the most intense moments of the whole cycle.
Planet Venus Rules Taurus, Libra Love, beauty, values
Planet Mars Rules Aries Action, energy, desire

Venus spends less of its time retrograde than any other planet. The rhythm is driven by the Venus synodic cycle, the time from one Sun-Venus conjunction of the same kind to the next, which is about 584 days, or roughly 19 months.
Frequency: about once every year and a half.
Duration: roughly 40 to 43 days of actual backward motion.
Share of time: about 7 percent. Around 1 in 14 people is born with Venus retrograde.
Effect on the calendar: in a normal year Venus moves through a sign in about a month. In a retrograde year it can stay in the same sign for around four months.

The most elegant feature is the eight-year pattern. Five Venus synodic cycles add up to almost exactly eight Earth years, only a couple of days short. So the retrogrades repeat in nearly the same part of the zodiac every eight years, a little earlier each time. If you plot the five inferior conjunctions around the zodiac, they trace a five-pointed star, the famous Venus pentagram. Practically, that means a Venus retrograde this year tends to echo the themes of the one eight years ago. If you want to know what a coming Venus retrograde will stir up, look at what was happening in your relationships or finances eight years earlier.
Mars has a longer cycle: its synodic period is about 780 days, a little over two years and one month.
Frequency: about every 26 months.
Duration: usually somewhere around two to two and a half months, though individual retrogrades can run a bit shorter or longer.
Share of time: roughly 9 to 10 percent, so about 1 in 10 people has Mars retrograde natally.
Effect on the calendar: Mars normally spends six or seven weeks in a sign. In a retrograde year it can spend several months in one or two signs.

Because Mars rules action, anger, competition, and physical energy, a long Mars retrograde is usually felt as friction on getting things moving. Projects stall and restart, old conflicts come back for a second round, and effort goes into revision rather than new ground.
Mars does not have a neat eight-year repetition the way Venus does. Its retrogrades move around the zodiac, falling in a different part of the sky each time.

muc.ten: How to read a retrograde transit
doan: A retrograde is a transit like any other; the difference is duration. The whole method is in transits explained, but here's how to handle Venus and Mars specifically.

Find the retrograde zone. Note the degree where the planet stations retrograde and the degree where it stations direct. The span between them is the zone the planet crosses three times: forward, backward, then forward again.

Find the shadow. The degrees that Venus or Mars will cover before the station retrograde (the pre-shadow) and after the station direct until it leaves the zone (the post-shadow). The whole shadow period for Mars can stretch to half a year or more.

Locate the house. Which of your houses does the zone fall in? That's the life area under review. Venus retrograde through your 7th house puts partnerships on the table. Mars retrograde through your 10th makes career effort feel stop-start.
Check contacts to natal planets. Any natal planet or angle inside the zone gets hit up to three times. These are the biggest parts of the retrograde for you personally.
Watch the stations. A station within about a degree of a natal planet or angle is the strongest signature. The planet sits there for days.

Suppose Venus stations retrograde at 25 degrees of Leo and stations direct at 10 degrees of Leo. (Real stations vary; this is for illustration.) Your natal Moon is at 15 degrees Leo in your 5th house, and your Ascendant is at 11 degrees Aquarius.

On the way forward, Venus crosses your Descendant at 11 Leo and then conjoins your Moon at 15 Leo. This first pass usually feels pleasant or at least noticeable: a new attraction, a creative impulse, some softness around home and feelings.

Venus stations at 25 Leo and turns back. It crosses 15 Leo again while retrograde. Now the Moon contact returns with a question attached. The attraction gets second-guessed, an old flame reappears, or money spent on pleasure gets reconsidered.

Venus stations direct at 10 Leo, which is 1 degree from your Descendant (the point opposite 11 Aquarius is 11 Leo). That station is the loudest moment for you: partnership questions sit on the table for several days.
Venus then moves forward over 11 and 15 Leo a third time. That's the resolution: the decision gets made, the relationship is renegotiated, the purchase finally happens or doesn't.
The same logic works for Mars, only slower, with the themes shifted toward effort, conflict, and drive.

muc.ten: Born with Venus or Mars retrograde
doan: A natal retrograde doesn't make the planet weaker in any simple sense. It tends to make that planet's function more internal, more considered, or slower to show itself. The general approach is in retrograde planets in the natal chart.

Natal Venus retrograde often describes someone whose values and tastes don't match the mainstream, who takes a long time to trust affection, or who revisits old relationships more than most. Many people with this placement say they understood what they actually wanted in love only after a few rounds of getting it wrong.

Natal Mars retrograde often shows as drive that runs inward. Anger may be held or processed slowly rather than expressed on the spot, and effort comes in bursts after long preparation. These people frequently do their best work when they revise something rather than start it fresh.

Look at secondary progressions too. Because progressed planets move one day per year of life, a natal retrograde Venus or Mars may station direct by progression at some point, and that year often marks a turn in how the person uses the planet. The method is in secondary progressions and the progressed Moon.

Treating the retrograde as a blanket ban. Plenty of relationships start and plenty of contracts get signed under Venus or Mars retrograde. The retrograde tells you the matter will likely be reviewed, not that it's doomed.
Ignoring your own chart. A Mars retrograde that falls in a house with no natal planets and no angles is mild for you. Everyone reading the same horoscope column is not having the same experience.

Forgetting the shadow. The themes usually start in the pre-shadow, when the planet first crosses the degrees it will later retrace. People are often surprised that the issue began weeks before the official date.

Copying Mercury retrograde rules. Mercury is about communication and logistics. Venus is about value, pleasure, and relationships; Mars is about action and conflict. Backing up your files won't help much with a Mars retrograde.
Using wide orbs. For a triple-pass transit, stick to about a degree for the conjunction to count, and pay most attention to stations. Anything wider is noise.
